subject: hax
title: Summarization request advertises the full live tool set so the provider's cached prompt prefix survives; tool calls in the summary response are answered with [rejected] results, never executed, up to 4 attempts
evidence: src/compact.c:240-266 (comment: 'Advertising the normal tools preserves the provider's cached request prefix. Calls are rejected rather than executed because compaction must not mutate task state'), src/compact.c:208-210 (TOOL_CALL_REJECTION), src/compact.c:102 (COMPACT_MAX_ATTEMPTS)
one_why: The usual way to stop a compaction call from running tools is to send an empty tool list -- which changes the request prefix and blows the prompt cache on the very next request; keeping the tools advertised and rejecting calls instead is strictly cheaper and reuses the seeded concept from the execution side.

subject: hax
title: Aggregate image budget enforced at ingestion by dropping the just-read image, not degrading older ones, so all prior serialized requests stay byte-stable and the prefix cache survives
evidence: src/agent_loop.c:227-235 (comment: 'Dropping the just-read image (rather than degrading older ones at serialization) keeps prior requests byte-stable, so the provider prefix cache survives'), src/agent_tool.h agent_tool_result_enforce_image_budget call site
one_why: Monotonicity applied to multimodal content: budget decisions taken at append-time on the newest item only, so history bytes never mutate retroactively -- the cache-safe alternative to trim-on-serialize schemes.

subject: hax
title: No permission gate by explicit doctrine with a correct threat model: an in-process approval gate is declared 'not a security boundary' and isolation is delegated to container/VM, while the README repeats the omission to users
evidence: docs/philosophy.md:74-83 ('because it runs inside the process it guards, it is not a security boundary ... run hax in a container or VM'), README.md:33 ('per-command permission prompts, other agents build exactly that -- hax deliberately doesn't'), src/agent_core.c:51-53 (prompt-only git prohibitions), src/tools/bash_classify.h:6-7 (classifier 'never changes execution')
one_why: Same delegation posture the corpus flags as safety-hole (cline-7, pi), but stated up front instead of discovered -- the honest-minimalist pole of the permission design space; note the display-only classifier is explicitly NOT a phantom control.

subject: hax
title: Mock provider compiled into the shipped binary, scripted from plain-text files via env vars, so Python e2e tests drive the real CLI end-to-end under meson and C tests script loop/compact paths with in-process provider fakes
evidence: src/providers/mock.c (638 LOC), tests/e2e/harness.py:68-108 (HAX_PROVIDER=mock, HAX_MOCK_SCRIPT=scripts/mock/*.txt), tests/meson.build:151-166 (e2e registration), scripts/mock/{tool_roundtrip,tasks,interrupt_stall}.txt, tests/test_agent_loop.c:171-386
one_why: Zero-network deterministic e2e of the actual binary including interrupt and background-task scenarios; the script-file format doubles as the fixture language for --json output tests (test_oneshot_json.py).

subject: hax
title: Bash commands outliving their foreground window are adopted into a task registry owning the process tree, a drainer thread, a spool file, and a per-task cursor of what the model has already seen; completion notes inject at the earliest loop seams
evidence: src/tools/task_registry.h:8-30 (adoption contract), src/tools/task_registry.h:44-58 (task_wait_stream with kill escalation SIGTERM-grace-SIGKILL), src/agent_loop.c:292-300 (task_collect_notes delivered before the request is built)
one_why: Turn-start note injection plus a delivery cursor means long builds never block the loop and the model never re-reads output it has seen -- no other subject has an adoption (rather than launch) model for background work.

subject: hax
title: Append-only versioned JSONL journal where /undo appends a cut record instead of truncating, files flush per newline for tail -f, and torn final lines after a crash are repaired on resume with a test
evidence: docs/sessions.md:22-24 ('append-only and flushed at each newline ... /undo appends a record rather than truncating'), tests/test_session.c:505-529 (test_resume_repairs_torn_final_line), tests/test_session.c:389-402 (resume appends only new items)
one_why: Undo-as-journal-entry (not file rewrite) keeps the same bytes a third-party tail saw, and the crash contract is stated for readers ('skip lines that do not parse') then tested -- nuance on the seeded journal id centered on append-only undo semantics.

subject: hax
title: A philosophy doc answering 'why not X' for each shipped-elsewhere feature (MCP, hooks, permission prompts, slash commands, deps), including an explicit statement of what the design cannot express
evidence: docs/philosophy.md:39-113; honest-gap line at :47-72 ('What outside scripts cannot express is in-turn interception ... hax omits that deliberately rather than claiming a substitute')
one_why: The written answer converts scope-minimalism from a README claim into a reviewable design record, and the admission of the uncovered gap (no veto/rewrite between tool call and next request) is what keeps it honest rather than marketing.
